A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ShieldAgent work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing additions to be distinguished from relocated or renumbered material.

before.justification: Section 5 and Tables 2–7 report original guardrail evaluations, including accuracy, false positives, rule recall, inference costs, and online policy compliance. Appendix C also reports policy-optimization diagnostics.

after.justification: The original empirical evaluations remain, and new Table 8 reports policy-model statistics before and after optimization across six environments.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithms 1–3, and the training and inference equations are retained. The new action-hierarchy and tool-call examples expand documentation of the existing workflow without establishing a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ShieldAgent-Bench, ST-WebAgentBench, VWA-Adv, and AgentHarm with the same environment and risk coverage. The added optimization statistics and Reddit example concern environments and safety requirements already covered.

E2.justification: Direct, Rule Traverse, and GuardAgent retain the same participation in corresponding comparisons. The unshielded AWM agent also remains the reference in the online evaluation; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The stated benchmark metrics, comparison controls, and offline and online evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Table 8 newly specifies a ten-iteration optimization limit, but this disclosure does not establish a changed experimental budget.

E4.justification: New Table 8 extends the existing GitLab optimization diagnostics with before-and-after statistics across all six environments. Figures 7 and 11–19 add illustrative refinement, pruning, and Reddit privacy-violation case studies, providing a limited supplementary extension.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The removed Table 7 statement about alternating ±0.1 perturbations describes numerical adjustment, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Benchmark results in Tables 2–7 remain numerically unchanged. New Table 8 adds optimization results, including Shopping predicates decreasing from 920 to 461, rules from 562 to 240, and average vagueness from 0.71 to 0.38; these are supplementary results rather than improved benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The LTL definitions, probabilistic model, relative safety condition, and training loss are unchanged. Added rule instances and verification-code examples illustrate existing mathematics without introducing new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about policy-grounded agent shielding, ShieldAgent-Bench, and superior guardrail accuracy and efficiency. The added appendix material does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Figure 12 adds a specific mechanism explanation linking GDPR-specific predicates to selecting an appropriate checking tool. Table 7 also loses the qualification that its scores were perturbed, affecting interpretation of unchanged results. The main robustness discussion and hallucination-related qualification remain.

D1.justification: New examples supply annotation fields, hierarchical action matching, MCP calls, predicate assignments, Prover9/Mace4 verification, and an illustrative threshold of 0.1. Table 8 discloses the ten-iteration limit. Conversely, Table 7 removes the perturbation and arithmetic-mean disclosure; existing algorithms, prompts, and project access information remain.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive related-work positioning are unchanged. Removing repeated citations from Tables 6–7 does not remove those works from the paper or change its relationship to them.

P1.justification: The main narrative, section sequence, and prompt templates are largely verbatim. Changes include explanatory appendix captions and worked-example narration, shortened table captions, an acknowledgment addition, conference information, and relocation of the project link into the abstract.

P2.justification: The appendix substantially expands its visual exposition with an annotated trajectory, refinement and pruning illustrations, a multistage shielding walkthrough, and a new statistics table. Existing optimization plots and policy examples are retained but relocated or renumbered, rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The optimization statistics and worked examples improve explanatory coverage. However, v2 removes Table 7's disclosure that the unchanged AgentHarm scores were perturbed, reducing transparency. Its new walkthrough also changes data_is_harmful from false in Figure 16 to true in Figure 17 without explanation. With central experimental results unchanged, the documentation gains and new consistency concerns leave the net quality effect uncertain.
